entries.originalText:
Lily: Hi Tom! Our teacher asked us to prepare a speech about volunteers. I think it’s a big
topic — where should we start?
Tom: I totally agree! Talking about all volunteers is too broad. (1) Many of us want to
volunteer but don’t know how.
Lily: (2) Teen volunteers have special needs, like safety and time for homework. Let’s
narrow it down to “what teens should note when volunteering.”
Tom: I couldn’t agree more. (3) My cousin got lost alone at a clean–up.
Lily: Hmm. Safety should always be first. What’s more, teens shouldn’t spend too much time —
my friend skipped class and failed a test.
Lily: Right! (4)
Tom: (5) I’m sure that will be very useful.
Lily: Perfect! Let’s act at once.
A. That’s a great idea!
B. Balance is better than cutting time.
C. Maybe we can focus on teenagers?
D. It might inspire more students to take action.
E. Add our stories as examples — classmates will get it easily.
F. Teens must choose safe activities.

阅读短文及文后选项, 选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。
Twenty–six years ago, David went deep into the rainforest and got lost for three weeks. But
he got out of the forest successfully (1)
David always wanted to travel in a rainforest. Later, he and his friend Ken, started out
together.
(2) So they built a boat and started. When they went near a waterfall, they fell
into the water. (3) David then spent four days trying to find his friend but he couldn’t.
During this time, some fishermen saved Ken. He quickly went to the town and asked for help
from the people there.
Deep in the forest. David was lost and alone. Also he found some dangerous animals around.
As the days passed, David had no food and became ill. (4)
One day, David heard the sound of a boat engine. He tried his best to get to the river bank
（河岸）. (5) Together, they finally saved David.
A. Ken swam to the bank but David was rushed down the river.
B. Their plan was to travel on a boat down a big river.
C. The question is——how did he do that?
D. It was Ken and the rescue group on the boat.
E. He wanted to give up many times.

A: Hey, Jake, did I do something wrong earlier?
B: No, not at all! (1)
A: Well, you had your arms crossed and didn’t really look at me when I was talking.
B: Oh, I’m so sorry, Emma. (2) I was just tired.
A: (3) It doesn’t matter.
B: But I should pay more attention. I didn’t mean to make you feel bad.
A: (4) I’m glad you explained.
B: Thanks for understanding. Next time, I won’t cross my arms and I will look at you in your eyes
when you talk.
A: Haha, that’s a good idea. (5)
B: Exactly. If I ever seem off (看起来不对劲) again, just ask me what’s wrong.
A: Okay. (6)
B: Agreed.
A. I see.
B. Don’t worry about it.
C. I didn’t mean to do that.
D. Why do you say so?
E. Communication solves many problems.
F. Body language can say a lot of things when we talk.
